title: [59F] intense sharp pain in left side of neck that comes and goes
selftext:
59F, 5’3, 140 pounds, Asian, taking simvastatin 10mg for high cholesterol, no smoking or drinking

Asking on behalf of my mother. She’s been experiencing pain in her neck for many months now and still hasn’t gotten a proper diagnosis despite so many trips to the hospital. 

Initially the pain was rather mild, and not as frequent. She went to the ENT specialist, and they found nothing after an X-ray. They sent her home with omeprazole, thinking it could be acid reflux. The omeprazole didn’t help, and she went back to the hospital, this time they made her do a CT thyroid scan. They found 2 nodules on her thyroid, one 0.4cm and one 1cm wide. The doctor said at this point there was nothing they could do, and told her to come back in 6 months’ time to check on the nodules again. They also did an endoscopy and found nothing. Again, they gave her omeprazole and some Difflam gargle. She still experienced some mild pain some days, but it wasn’t too bad. 

Fast forward 2 months later to early October, she suddenly experienced intense pain like she has never experienced before in the left side of her neck. It’s the kind of pain that renders her unable to move or speak. She would clutch at her neck and scrunch her face in pain. She describes the pain as one that shoots up to her jaw. It lasts for about 10-15 seconds each time, and after that she’s completely fine. No traces of pain anywhere. And this same pattern occurs about at least 10+ times in one day. We brought her to another hospital, and they said it might be a pinched nerve. They gave her gabapentin and a ton of painkillers (paracetamol, tramadol, etoricoxib) and famotidine and gave her a follow-up appointment to the neurologist. 

She’s been taking these medicines for 4 days now and has seen no improvement in the pain. The painkillers don’t help as well. Her appointment with the neuroscience department isn’t until November and she doesn’t think she can tolerate the pain till then. I’m very worried about her. 

What could the problem be?

Edit: Thank you all so much for your input and concern. I’ll update this post if there’s any development, in case it could help anyone experiencing similar issues.

Edit 2: Hi all, I’m finally updating this months later. My mother never got a proper diagnosis, but the methycobal and gabapentin she was on seemed to help. She has not experienced the pain since then. But unfortunately, one of her thyroid nodules has been found to be malignant and she’s getting a partial thyroidectomy soon. The specialist she saw said the thyroid nodules have nothing to do with the pain she experienced though. Praying that the surgery will go smoothly.

title: Trying to find the best medication to treat Generalized Anxiety Disorder and PTSD without worsening sexual dysfunction or causing weight gain
selftext:
Very specific question incoming.  Wanted to get a preliminary idea of what the options really are before we go make a psych appointment.  I am a medical student at a MD school in the southern US using a throwaway account to ask this question on behalf of my wife.  I have tried to find answers to this everywhere; my textbooks, UpToDate, Dynamed, Wikipedia, etc.  I do know some psychiatrists from my psych clerkship but don't really want to ask this question in person to them due to the personal nature of this situation.  The history is below for some context, but basically she is in therapy and doing well, and I believe that medication would help a great deal but we haven't been to a psychiatrist yet.  We want to find the best medication that would treat Generalized Anxiety Disorder (first and foremost), as well as PTSD, without making her sexual dysfunction worse than it is now.  I'm aware that GAD and PTSD are generally treated with SSRIs or SNRIs, but these medications are notorious for their sexual side effect profile.  Additionally, I know that Bupropion is the antidepressant with the least sexual side effects that you would move to next after SSRIs for most of the disorders that SSRIs treat, but it appears that there is no evidence of Bupropion being an effective treatment for GAD; other non-sexual side effect antidepressant drugs like Vortioxetine or Vilazodone have a similar story.  I'm aware that Mirtazapine can be used to treat GAD and doesn't really cause sexual side effects, but my wife has been trying very hard to lose weight recently by exercising frequently (180 lbs mostly adipose tissue to 170 lbs mostly lean body mass in the last year, yay!) and does not want to take something that is know to commonly cause weight gain (like Mirtazapine.)  So what would be a good option for her?  Is there another drug that I'm unaware of that would treat GAD, PTSD, and not worsen sexual side effects or cause weight gain?  Or should she try an SSRI/SNRI and see if it affects her sex drive?  Or should she try Mirtazapine and see if it affects her weight?  

History: My wife (25yo F) has had Generalized Anxiety Disorder for her entire life that was diagnosed a couple years ago.  Additionally, she has PTSD from an episode of sexual assault at age 18.  She has been seeing a therapist for these issues approximately twice a month for a little less that one year.  Due to both of these conditions and the nature of her assault she has been dealing with significant anxiety around anything to do with sexuality, and is specifically avoidant of penises (all penises, not just my own, before anybody decides to make jokes) as they are somewhat of a "trigger" for her anxiety.  Basically the only time that we are ever intimate is after we have both been drinking (don't worry, we've discussed consent at great length while sober and both agreed that we're fine with everything in the bedroom after some drinks and we know our boundaries, etc.), because it is the only time that she can overcome her anxiety about intimacy.  99% of the time, our intimacy is me pleasuring her and then her apologizing that she is not able to do the same to me, which I am perfectly ok with as I know that it will take a significant amount of time and therapy for this issue to be resolved.  She is in therapy, 2x per month for a year, mainly CBT and EMDR.  Has not tried any medication so far.

I went to the urgent care across the street where they took x-rays and scheduled me for a follow-up the next day. The medications did not help my symptoms. I could not be in or around the pool area because within minutes I would feel the same sensation I did when I first had the exposure. I was still experiencing severe coughing fits that led to upper chest pain and a sore throat. Such fits would last for over an hour even after removing myself from the irritant (which included the pool, cleaning chemicals, and some perfumes). 

My second follow-up visit, I told the care provider that my symptoms weren't improving. She did a basic exam of my breathing and throat, said I looked fine and would be able to return to work, then rushed out the door. I tried to continue to work, but I was still experiencing the symptoms listed above and would constantly have to leave work early because of them.

LUNG VOLUMES: normal based on total lung capacity of 99% predicted.   
MECHANICS: Normal FEV1/FVC ratio of 79 with a FEV1 of 104% predicted.   
DIFFUSION CAPACITY: Moderately reduced based on a DLCO of 67% predicted. 

During my follow-up, the pulmonologist said all of my results were normal and would not give me an answer as to why I'm still experiencing coughing fits and upper chest pain when around a "trigger substance." He didn't have an answer for me and said "I don't know what you want me to say, you should be fine."

I went for a second opinion, this time with an ENT. I figured if my lungs are fine, then it must be my throat that's injured. 

The ENT used a camera to look at my throat, and said I have a lot of bumps in the back of my throat (I think he said cobblestoning). He said it was hard for him to tell how my injury played a part in my throat's condition; but what possibly happened is, because I have a history of post nasal drip/acid reflux, the chlorine only exacerbated my throat's condition, which is why I'm still sensitive to chemicals. But then he immediately followed up that statement with, "I see patients with the same throat condition as mine without my injury, so I can't say for sure if the chlorine did damage or not." 

He treated me for my post nasal drip and reflux with prescriptions (haven't picked them up yet), and I have a follow up in 4 weeks. When I asked him again why I'm still feeling symptoms, he didn't say anything about it and focused the visit on treating my acid reflux/PND.

No one is saying anything about why I'm still feeling the way I am. They're either saying they have no clue or that I should be fine. I've been in and around pools for all of my life, I was a competitive swimmer for eight years, and I was an opera singer for four years after that. Never have I had any issues with breathing or being around chemicals until December 14th. 

My partner still works at a pool, and if I get near his wet uniform, within five minutes I'll begin to have a coughing fit that makes it difficult for me to breathe, and I'll experience upper chest pain. This will last for an hour or more. I've had to change all my cleaning chemicals to vinegar, baking soda, and soap. I can't be around chemicals of any kind. I have to use very specific hand sanitizer because most brands affect me. 

I don't know if I'll ever be able to swim again. I was in and around the water for more than a decade. My livelihood was based in aquatics. Now I can't be anywhere near any of that. None of this is normal for me, and over four months after the incident, no one can tell me why I'm still feeling this way. I'm at my wit's end. 

What's wrong with me? Why does every medical professional I see give me a different answer or tell me nothing should be wrong? It's clear something is not right, and it's hard for me to deny the correlation between the incident and my current condition. *Something* clearly happened to me, but no one is telling me what. Can anyone tell me where to go from here? What happened to me on December 14th? What specialist can help me diagnose my condition? Will I ever be able to get back to my normal life?

I'm sorry if I sound frantic or pushy. I'm worried about my condition, and exhausted from trying to pursue these elusive answers to my questions. Thank you in advance to anyone that answers this.

selftext:

I closed my finger in our home door 4 days ago. Immediate bruising occurred, but I did not realize how bad the bruising and swelling would get. Ty

title: My breast reduction is healing strangely 6 months post-op; what should I do?
selftext:
I \[ 20F, 163cm, 72kg, Pakistani \] had a breast reduction & areola reduction back in late June 2022. The journey has been very messy & too much happened to recall. I was told it would take 10 days for me to fully recover & start showering but that was NOT the case.

Right from day 1, I had nonstop fevers. This lasted for around five days. Lost 3kg from the fever alone. 

Day 7, I was oozing really really badly through my thick dressing so I went to get my dressing changed for the first time. Within an hour of getting home, I had already oozed through the dressing and both bras I was wearing.

For a solid 3 months, I had to change my dressing 3 - 5 times a day because the discharge would leak through many layers of gauze, surgical tape, two bras & my shirt. All the doctor prescribed was a nitril spray ( which is for angina & you spray into your mouth? But doctor suspected nipple death so he'd tell me to spray onto my nipples . . . )

My wound was healing really slowly & I think they overestimated the elasticity of my skin because my skin just kept ripping apart & creating new wounds all across the suture lines. I must've visited the surgeon 15+ times & every single time, they assured me nothing was wrong. 

Two months in, I had itchy skin due to irritation from bandages so doctor lathered my wound in magnesium sulfate paste. IMMEDIATELY, it started to burn & it took us an hour to get home. As soon as I got home, immediately peeled off the dressing to see hundreds of boils & burns all over my chest. Doctor said this was normal, just to apply Betnovate N Cream but other doctors recommended Fucidic Acid; the latter was the only ointment that worked. 

Then, a few weeks later, my oozing had turned green. At this point, only my surgeon was changing my dressing since the wounds were going open too much. I googled what it meant & green discharge means pus. Asked the surgeon if this was any cause for concern, he said no. I asked if I should do a pus culture, he said no again.

A few days later, we moved from Karachi to Quetta ( though we will return to Karachi every few months ). I went to a hospital to get a pus culture & they detected Pseudomonas in both my breasts. Sent my doctor my results, only for him to say medication wasn't necessary, just Betnovate N Cream only for me to research and find out Betnovate N Cream makes Pseudomonas infections WORSE. Unfortunately, a disastrous flood happened in Quetta & I couldn't access the hospital for three weeks. 

By now, I was constantly feeling very ill & dizzy, passing out & got rushed to a hospital. I was on antibiotic IVs for about a full week & had nearly gone into septic shock. After this, my doctor started to ghost me. 

Thankfully, most of my issues are better now ( except maybe the hypertrophic scarring but that's okay ), just that there's this bleeding flesh about an inch underneath my nipple. Considering I have no contact with my surgeon & can't find any breast surgeons near me, they don't know what this is. What is this, why did it happen & do I need to stitch this up or can ointments close this wound up? I took this picture just an hour ago.

[https://imgur.com/a/iBsMll8](https://imgur.com/a/iBsMll8)

title: Reddit, should I be concerned?
selftext:
I know damn well that a lot of people - especially teenagers my age - tend to question their health, rely on diagnoses, and overthink, but I'd appreciate some feedback. I know it's long, but please please please help if you can. 

( If you don't want to read it, at least click on the link and listen to the video of my mouth. It'll freak you out. Luv u ♥️ )

I'm a 16 year old female. I'm 5'5 and weigh about 105 pounds. I'm half Filipino(mom) and half American(dad). My mom is of latino descent. I usually take 60mg of Dextroamphetamine(Adderall XR) in the morning, 1mg of Prazosin(Minipress) at night, birth control, and Sertraline(Zoloft). I'm not sure if this is relevant, but heart, lung, sleep, and brain problems are very common in both sides of my family. My dad actually had a brain tumor that hemorrhaged, which is cool. (Dad, if you see this, hi! Get off Reddit and hug me, damn it.)

Anyways, my main concerns are my excessive sleepiness and shortness of breath. Now, I know what you're probably thinking. 

A teenager? Tired? How UNIQUE and CONCERNING! 

It's a bit more than that, though. I'm SO TIRED. 
But this is fairly recent. And it's getting worse. I just kinda want some tips and coping mechanisms with my excessive sleepiness, though, so if you don't care about that please skip to my shortness of breath paragraph. I just hope that my tiredness isn't related to my heart or lungs or anything.


Short backstory: Last September, I underwent a very traumatic event and was raped. The trauma really didn't end there, though. It dragged on until June 2018 due to  constant harassment and threats. From September - December 2017, i rarely slept. I'm talking about a ridiculously small amount of sleep - around 2 hours worth every 3 or 4 days. During this period of temporary insomnia, I was having intense hallucinations and was going to counseling for my PTSD. At some point, though, my body had had enough sleep deprivation, and I was unable to stay awake for ANYTHING. I was then prescribed Prazosin, Sertraline, and Adderall. I was thought to potentially have narcolepsy, since it runs in my dad's family. Since then, I've struggled with extreme fatigue and tiredness.

Today I recieved my sleep study and polysomnogram results, which were not consistent with narcolepsy. I DO have an incredibly fast sleep onset, though, and can sleep within 2 minutes. This was relieving but has me wondering if my excessive sleepiness is trauma induced. Can anyone conclude this? Besides managing a sleep schedule, how do I combat my sleepiness? Is this normal? I've fallen asleep driving(while stopped in traffic), in every class hour almost every day, while talking, eating, typing, walking, etc. I have constant sleepwalking and talking episodes, but my PSG showed no REM abnormalities. My dad wants to lower my adderall dosage, but I'm barely managing on 60mg. I don't know how to begin to convey my tiredness. I have cataplexy-like episodes of muscle weakness and fatigue when stressed or physically exerted, and fall asleep almost immediately after. Ultimately I'm mainly concerned about my grades, safety, and presentation since I'm always drowsy. I just want to cope and not have it interfere with my daily life. I usually sleep at about 10:30pm and wake up at 7, but I'm often exhausted and sleep even earlier. :( However, I nap a lot during the day and try to avoid napping past 4. It's probably just how I deal with stress, but the sleepiness itself stresses me out even more. What else can I even do? At least if I had narcolepsy I'd have solid answers. The best advice they had for me was to correct my sleeping schedule, but I shit you not I've slept for days and still felt uncontrollably tired.  It's very frustrating to sleep through things I don't want to miss. It's very frustrating to know I can dismiss puzzle alarms in my sleep. It's frustrating to know that when I sleep talk I say things I don't mean. My dad punched a hole in my door because I was conversing with him while asleep, lmao. I don't even know what I want anymore. 


NOW FOR MY NEXT AND MORE IMPORTANT CONCERN! 

 It's actually more important than the sleepiness, so sorry for the long paragraphs. 

Short backstory: When I was 8, I used an inhaler as needed because i lived in SLC and the smog was terrible. I didn't use it much at all though. 

I moved to a different place in Utah without smog in January 2017 and completely forgot about my inhaler.

 However, since about March I've become increasingly fatigued and out of breath. It's gotten really bad lately and I was prescribed my inhaler again. It doesn't help much. At all. My peak flow chart does increase, though... My doctor doesn't know if it's asthma or not.

I wouldn't be too concerned except I've also developed an externally audible heartbeat in my mouth. I can't stand up or roll over without wheezing, and my heartbeat is very fast. My muscles become weak and I almost collapse if I don't catch my breath. It is audible when my mouth is closed, but it is a lot louder when my mouth is open. In a silent room, you can hear it from about 5 feet away. This happens with any exertion, all day, every day. The heartbeat thing started in June or July. Since then, my muscle weakness and shortness of breath have been worse than ever. 

Here is a video of my heartbeat!
 https://photos.app.goo.gl/qFaxrHAhWpNZXwxf7 

Ignore my disgusting mouth. I have other recordings, but this one's the clearest and it's easiest to see that it's in conjunction with my heart. 

This also interferes with my daily life. It sucks! I've had an EKG done a few months ago with no major concerns, and my lungs sound normal on a stethoscope. 

My adderall makes it a bit worse, but my heartbeat thing, weakness, and shortness of breath happens even without it. Same with the Prazosin and sertraline and birth control. I can't walk to one class to another without being late because I constantly have to catch my breath. :( I don't know how to combat this either. Is it something I should be concerned about? Because I'm kinda concerned. I just don't know what to do about it, since my inhaler doesn't help me much. Anyone have an explanation to what the hell the sound is? My lungs? My heart? It's probably nothing, but that coupled with muscle weakness, chest pain, and fatigue is enough to convince me it might be something else.  

What do y'all think? Should I be doing anything to treat this? Does anyone know what it is? Is it normal? Should I be watching out for anything? I don't know, I'm probably paranoid. It's just weird. And uncomfortable. I hate being so aware of my heart.

 I like freaking people out with my mouth, but at the end of the day, it freaks me out the most. I dunno. Any feedback would be cool, even if it's just "wtf ur heart sounds like 2 dudes banging." 

this probably didn't make much sense because i was half asleep writing some of this but yeah

TL,DR;

I usually take 60mg of Dextroamphetamine(Adderall XR) in the morning, 1mg of Prazosin(Minipress) at night, birth control, and Sertraline(Zoloft). I'm not sure if this is relevant, but heart, lung, sleep, and brain problems are very common in both sides of my family. My dad actually had a brain tumor that hemorrhaged, which is cool. Anyways, my main concerns are my excessive sleepiness and shortness of breath. Now, I know what you're probably thinking. 

A teenager? Tired? How UNIQUE and CONCERNING! 

It's a bit more than that, though. I'm SO TIRED. 
But this is fairly recent. And it's getting worse. I just kinda want some tips and coping mechanisms with my excessive sleepiness, though, so if you don't care about that please skip to my shortness of breath paragraph. I just hope that my tiredness isn't related to my heart or lungs or anything.


Short backstory: Last September, I underwent a very traumatic event and was raped. The trauma really didn't end there, though. It dragged on until June 2018 due to  constant harassment and threats. From September - December 2017, i rarely slept. I'm talking about a ridiculously small amount of sleep - around 2 hours worth every 3 or 4 days. During this period of temporary insomnia, I was having intense hallucinations and was going to counseling for my PTSD. At some point, though, my body had had enough sleep deprivation, and I was unable to stay awake for ANYTHING. I was then prescribed Prazosin, Sertraline, and Adderall. I was thought to potentially have narcolepsy, since it runs in my dad's family. Since then, I've struggled with extreme fatigue and tiredness.

Today I recieved my sleep study and polysomnogram results, which were not consistent with narcolepsy. I DO have an incredibly fast sleep onset, though, and can sleep within 2 minutes. This was relieving but has me wondering if my excessive sleepiness is trauma induced. Can anyone conclude this? Besides managing a sleep schedule, how do I combat my sleepiness? Is this normal? I've fallen asleep driving(while stopped in traffic), in every class hour almost every day, while talking, eating, typing, walking, etc. I have constant sleepwalking and talking episodes, but my PSG showed no REM abnormalities. Ultimately I'm mainly concerned about my grades, safety, and presentation since I'm always drowsy. I just want to cope and not have it interfere with my daily life. I usually sleep at about 10:30pm and wake up at 7, but I'm often exhausted and sleep even earlier. :( However, I nap a lot during the day and try to avoid napping past 4. It's probably just how I deal with stress, but the sleepiness itself stresses me out even more. What else can I even do? At least if I had narcolepsy I'd have solid answers. The best advice they had for me was to correct my sleeping schedule, but I shit you not I've slept for days and still felt uncontrollably tired.  It's very frustrating to sleep through things I don't want to miss. It's very frustrating to know I can dismiss puzzle alarms in my sleep. It's frustrating to know that when I sleep talk I say things I don't mean. My dad punched a hole in my door because I was conversing with him while asleep, lmao. I don't even know what I want anymore. 


NOW FOR MY NEXT AND MORE IMPORTANT CONCERN! 

 It's actually more important than the sleepiness, so sorry for the long paragraphs. 

Short backstory: When I was 8, I used an inhaler as needed because i lived in SLC and the smog was terrible. I didn't use it much at all though. 

I moved to a different place in Utah without smog in January 2017 and completely forgot about my inhaler.

 However, since about March I've become increasingly fatigued and out of breath. It's gotten really bad lately and I was prescribed my inhaler again. It doesn't help much. At all. My peak flow chart does increase, though... My doctor doesn't know if it's asthma or not.

My muscles become weak and I almost collapse if I don't catch my breath. It is audible when my mouth is closed, but it is a lot louder when my mouth is open. In a silent room, you can hear it from about 5 feet away. This happens with any exertion, all day, every day. The heartbeat thing started in June or July. Since then, my muscle weakness and shortness of breath have been worse than ever. 

Here is a video of my heartbeat!
 https://photos.app.goo.gl/qFaxrHAhWpNZXwxf7 

Ignore my disgusting mouth. I have other recordings, but this one's the clearest and it's easiest to see that it's in conjunction with my heart. 

This also interferes with my daily life. It sucks! I've had an EKG done a few months ago with no major concerns, and my lungs sound normal on a stethoscope. 

My adderall makes it a bit worse, but my heartbeat thing, weakness, and shortness of breath happens even without it. Same with the Prazosin and sertraline and birth control. I can't walk to one class to another without being late because I constantly have to catch my breath. :( I don't know how to combat this either. Is it something I should be concerned about? Because I'm kinda concerned. I just don't know what to do about it, since my inhaler doesn't help me much. Anyone have an explanation to what the hell the sound is? My lungs? My heart? It's probably nothing, but that coupled with muscle weakness, chest pain, and fatigue is enough to convince me it might be something else.  

What do y'all think? Should I be doing anything to treat this? Does anyone know what it is? Is it normal? Should I be watching out for anything? I don't know, I'm probably paranoid. It's just weird. And uncomfortable. I hate being so aware of my heart.

 I like freaking people out with my mouth, but at the end of the day, it freaks me out the most. I dunno. Any feedback would be cool, even if it's just "wtf ur heart sounds like 2 dudes banging."

title: Nodular acne turned into an abscess?
selftext: My story is kind of long and complicated. I’m an eighteen year old south-east Asian female. I was initially diagnosed with nodular acne. The doctor prescribed me with azithromycin and isotretinoin to be specific. After one week, the nodule had become soft and pus had form in it (abscess) and the doctor performed an I&D, but he tried to prick the skin to drain the pus as he was reluctant to make the incision given the fact the abscess is on my cheek. He prescribed the same medication as before and did not insert a wick inside. The very next morning, the pus had come back and the abscess had form again but this time more purple in colour, maybe due to the fact that he squeezed the skin a lot during the drainage. After few days, we went to another doctor who prescribed amoxicillin. The abscess changed slightly and the skin started to become dry around it. The doctor also tried to take out the pus through a syringe, the abscess diminished a significant amount but not completely. Eventually, the doctor performed another I&D. He said that I was suffering from anitibioma. Maybe the medication the first doctor prescribed me, didn’t suit me well and it caused a prolong abscess. The reason why I gave such a detailed description of my experience is because I’m really confused. How did an acne nodule went on to become a chronic abscess? What just happened? Was I doing something wrong? Was the doctor doing something wrong? Please help me, I’m terrified. I need some insight. Thanks.

title: Adderall "calm": myth or undiagnosed adhd?
selftext:
Demographic info: 22F, asian, 5'3" and 50kg, current meds are 60mg fluoxetine, long psychiatric history. I drink, smoke, and use recreational drugs. 

I took 20 mg Adderall XR yesterday for the first time in my life when offered by a close friend with diagnosed ADHD. He was with me for the whole day and is the reason why I'm asking, because he thinks my reaction indicates undiagnosed ADHD. He actually was diagnosed because his strange reactions to off the street stimulants and a prior mental health history prompted him to reach out to his doctor (vvyanse, adderall, and coke). I have an extremely similar mental health background as well (being mood disorders, anxiety disorders, eating disorders). 

It had unexpected effects for me: I felt extremely and unusually calm. I work from home and I found work was easier to do, but I didn't feel compelled to be super productive like I've heard adderall is supposed to
make you (it was a Friday and I was all caught up for the week anyways). I did a regular amount of work in a day but it was less anxiety inducing than usual I suppose. It was like time and my brain slowed down. 

Now, I tried to do some googling and there are some people who claim it's an urban myth that becoming calm on adderall = undiagnosed adhd. So, is it? 
I'm hesitant to ask either my doctor or my counselor because I don't want to be labeled as a "substance user" on my psych records

selftext:
Looking for any help. I'm a 29 year old fit and healthy female with a good diet, Non-smoker and rarely drink and I have had thrush for well over a year. When I first noticed symptoms I went to the doctors who confirmed thrush. I got transferred to a sexual health clinic who also tested for chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis including a range of other things as well as thrush, thrush again was confirmed and all other tests came back negative. I was put on fluconazole for 3 months at a low dose. It was confirmed at my check up after 3 months I still had thrush so was put on a higher dose for 3 more months, I also asked for more tests at the time but nurse said it was unnecessary. Hopeful the symptoms would disappear I have left the country to travel. Well its over 6 months after I finished treatment and I still very much have thrush, although now it is a lot harder to just pop to the doctors. I have tried EVERYTHING I know... Chinese medicine, Tea Tree oil, Oregano oil, Coconut oil, Lemon juice, garlic, I cut sugar (all sugar, even fruit) from my diet for over a week, replaced all my underwear with cotton, I sleep with no undies on, I avoid wearing jeans, been taking pro biotic for months, all kinds of creams, gels from the pharmacy, and thrush pills. On a good note the only symptom I have is a small amount of discharge but it is still enough to require a change of undies twice a day. Before I was diagnosed I basically had no discharge. I have changed sexual partners since and I'm currently in a long distance so no change of continual re-infection. Has anyone experienced this. I am truly at a loss.

Note: I forgot to say I've had the mirena for just under two years now. Could this be effecting it? I do not have a menstrual cycle.

selftext:
I wanted to state to begin with, someone wanted to push it being genetic like kleinfelters or kallmans syndrome. Seeing as a full genetic screening can cost upwards of ten thousand dollars and no one in my families has any genetic disorders, along with my testicles and body developing to a normal size and going through puberty it is NOT A GENETIC DISORDER.DONT SUGGEST IT, DONT THINK IT. It's not that i'm in denial, i just HIGHLY HIGHLY HIGHLY think it ISN'T. If i did i would've gotten ALL the tests done. On to the meat and potatoes.

&#x200B;

 

Excuse my bad grammar and all that jazz, i'm super tired writing this. 25 YO male concerned about fertility and decreasing testosterone levels. Have some bloodwork and basic stuff.

Over the past 4-5 years i've had steadily decreasing testosterone levels and slow testicle shrinkage (shown in ultrasounds i've lost about a CM in size in total of my testicles) / atrophy.

My testosterone level when all of this was first getting sorted out was 760-800 i believe. This was at around 21 years old. I'm now 25 and it's dropped to 530. Also, i can't remember what my FREE T was (and there's another male sex hormone) but that had dropped as well. I wanna state that TECHNICALLY throughout this whole time all my levels fell within the NORMAL range BUT they were always on the " Hey that's barely acceptable, and you're also only a 25 year old man not a 75 year old man" ALSO you gotta think for those "ranges" for testosterone most super healthy fertile active 25 YO's won't be getting testosterone tests done. So it's safe to assume those ranges probably even gear more towards older men to begin with. Plus they're vague and my symptoms (loss of muscle mass, thinner facial hair, constantly tired and weak.) have gotten worse from 21 to 25 years old.

The other thing is my semen analysis. At 22 i had it done. My levels all again "barely" fell within the vague ranges they give, but again, i was 22 at the time. I had like 30 million motile sperm and 96% were morphologically abnormal. The kruger values i believe say 4% is the cut-off limit. My moility was like 70% and like i said the count was 30 million. Leukoctyes was average-ish or lower, not a lot. Not a 40 YO man trying to knockup his 20 year old asian sweetheart. Also, fertility issues generally do NOT run in any of my families and i had a SHARP decrease in testosterone and how i felt from age 18 to age 22 and then to 25. Which i understand teens usually have the highest levels, but this was drastic feeling.

Haven't had a follow-up at 25 but something tells me it's probably now in the ABNORMAL range because it was barely normal then, and the only difference is my testosterone has had about a 300 point fucking drop in 3 years along with slightly smaller testicles. The only thing ultrasounds have shown ( i've had quite a few) are minor hydroceles and minor varicoceles which my doctor said not only are varicoceles usually significant when it comes to fertility but they only seriously affect it when noticeable and palpable and mine are not big at all. Negative for stds and all the common viral shit.

Along with my 530 testosterone level at age 25 (which according to studies i read usually its around 700 for guys this age, or a bit higher even.) i had a lower FSH and LH. FSH was 2.4 and LH was 3.6. I know those aren't "that low" or someone might even say average but combine that with a mediocre testosterone level and i've been trying since age 21 to concieve with no luck and something tells me theres an issue.

I know clomid can be taken off-label for mens fertility but it can raise "E2" levels and so anastrozole or an estrogen blocker is recommended with it.

Could i have a cortisol or pituitary issue? Could anything explain these issues? Don't say genetics, because not only is everyone in all my families very fertile but i've felt the decrease and like something has been "wrong" since i was around 21. Maybe a slow growing pituitary tumor? But then my prolactin would be off, and my prolactin is completely normal. Could it be an estrogenic tumor i do have gynecomastia and symptoms related to HIGH estrogen.

title: Consistent but minimal rectal bleeding
selftext:
21, Male, 65kg, UK

For about a month now, I've been regularly seeing a minimal amount of blood in my underwear from my nether region (with no pain whatsoever). My definition of minimal is a 2-3 long, faint, streaks of red blood (not brown, black or tar-like). I have a GP appointment booked soon (was the first available believe it or not) and have phoned 111 (the non-emergency UK health service) who advised that it's nothing to worry about as it's minimal and red, just to get a GP appointment - but naturally I am worrying. 

It seemed to have stopped for 2 days recently until I went to IKEA to get some new furniture. When I finished building, there was a considerable amount of blood but still not loads (not enough to fill a mug as 111 say). Since then, I am back to the minimal streaks and I am also slightly constipated. It seems that whenever I do any heavy activity, I bleed more heavily.

When I feel around my anus, there are 2-3 bumps, almost acne-like. When I put my finger on top of them, sometimes there is blood (a tiny amount like almost negligible) and sometimes my finger is completely dry.

What I want to know is what are the potential causes for this and how can I treat this? From what I've understood (please correct me if I'm wrong):

* Red blood means its surface level and not intestinal which is usually a good sign 
* Haemorrhoids/piles can be internal and external and usually involve pain (I have no pain)
* Haemorrhoids/piles can be treated permanently but not always
* Rectal bleeding can be but is not always a sign of colorectal cancer

Thank you in advance!

title: Ophthalmologists please help! My mom’s eyes are forcing her to live in the dark.
selftext:
TDLR: My mom has had severe pain from light sensitivity for about 6 months (to the point that she cannot drive, go outside in daylight, or even open the fridge because of the lights most days). When exposed to light: pain shoots through her left eye socket, migraine-like headache, sinuses back up immediately on the left side, left ear pops, and pain at the base of her skull on the left side. Her left eye is the worst and has an amniotic lens (right eye hardly better). 

She’s been tested and treated with various meds but they think the root problem is cornea inflammation. Because she is allergic to most steroids which typically treat this, they’re unsure what else to do. Please weigh in with any possible diseases to test for or meds to try! She’s in so much pain and lives states away from family so it is very difficult to get by alone without sight. TIA! 

- Age: 54 
- Sex: F 
- Current diagnoses: Severe dry eye syndrome, inflamed corneas 
- Current medications: Amniotic lense (bandage lens) in left eye is replaced every 2 weeks for the past ~5 months, serum tears every 2 hours, Xiidra 2 times daily, Moxifloxacin eye drops every 4 hours in the left eye with the lens, Retaine complete dry eye relief hourly or as needed. 
- Past/unsuccessful medications: Erythromycin, anti-inflammatory eye drops (type unknown), steroid eye drops, Restasis, doxycycline. 

She has had the following tests: 
- Thyroid: all normal levels  
- CT scan of head: negative for any pressure behind eyes 
- Blood test: all normal levels 
- Sjoregn’s syndrome/autoimmune: negative 

Timeline of treatment so far: 
- September 2023: Dry, itchy eyes. Optometrist prescribed antibiotic and a light steroid for 7 days. Also prescribed heat 3-5 times daily and artificial tears. 
- October: Went back to optometrist with no improvement, told to continue same treatment. 
- November: Went to ophthalmologist, who prescribed Erythromycin and anti-inflammatory eye drops. This caused a severe allergic reaction with symptoms: extreme drainage, burning, swelling, black and blue burnt skin around eyes from drainage. After this, she could no longer drive a car. 
- November: Ophthalmologist prescribed steroid eye drops to stop allergic reaction. Within 3 eye drop doses, another severe allergic reaction: eyes swelled extremely and throat constricted with difficulty breathing. She took Benadryl to stop the reaction. Went to ER. Since this allergic reaction, the light sensitivity became severe and has stayed severe. 
- ER appointment November: Prescribed hydroxyzine 4 times daily for allergic reaction. Hydroxyzine helped: she could see for about 3 hours after each dose before light sensitivity came back. 
- December: Ophthalmologist referred to Basscom-Palmer hospital due to allergies to too many medications. 
- January: Basscom-Palmer finds cornea inflammation. Stopped all medications besides Retaine artificial tears. Prescribed Restasis, Retaine, heat 3-5 times daily, and doxycycline. 
- January-March: No improvement. 
- March: Basscom-Palmer prescribed amniotic lens (bandage lens) which has been replaced every 2 weeks since then. 
- April: Basscom-Palmer prescribed Moxifloxacin every 4 hours over amniotic lens, introduced Zatidor 2 times daily. Still pain from light sensitivity. 
- April: Went to Mayo Clinic for second opinion, sent back to Basscom-Palmer as Mayo could not treat symptoms. 
- June 1: Basscom-Palmer stopped Restasis, stopped doxycycline, and introduced Xiidra. 
-  June 1-21: Had great relief for about 3 weeks. Still light sensitivity, but less pain and less severe sensitivity. She could drive for the first time again. After 3 weeks, symptoms came back (extreme light sensitivity with severe pain). 
- Current (mid July): This has continued until current—amniotic lens no longer comforting, causes pain 24/7. Doctor said the eye surface is deteriorating on her left eye and to take Tylenol as needed for the pain. They just stopped Zatidor drops at the last appointment this week due to preservatives and deterioration of the eye surface. They are considering prescribing a silicone lens with saline in it. 

Any insight at all helps!! Please help guide us to getting her the right treatment so she can live her life again!

title: Should I get an x-ray for my broken finger?
selftext: I'm 20F, White Asian, 5'4, 130 lb. At my job 3 days ago, I was walking with a cart of 50+ pounds, slipped, and dropped the cart on my left middle finger. Since then it has been painful and has been purple and black. The fingernail is badly bruised, and it is swollen. I can't bend the top part. I went to a clinic where they said I probably didn't *need* an x ray, plus it would be expensive, so I chose not to get one. They said to buddy tape it and keep taking OTC pain meds. Today though, I talked with my boyfriend who had a similar injury, and he told me about workers' comp, and that he thinks I should get an x-ray because his finger was broken and he got a splint afterwards. After that conversation I decided to report the injury to my supervisors and I'm filing workers' comp, so the cost of the x-ray isn't really a concern anymore. I'm more worried about permanent finger deformity now. Should I get an x-ray as soon as possible? Is it necessary with this condition?

title: Does this sound like asthma?
selftext:
Hi everyone. I'm a 21F, Indian, 5'6", 98lbs. I've had this issue on and off pretty much my entire life. I always assumed I was just out of shape, but my symptoms have been progressively getting worse. I've had a cough every morning for 7 years, with thick mucus, shortness of breathe whenever I exert myself (even just walking from my car to work/home/etc), tightness in my chest, difficulty sleeping, and pressure on my chest when I lay down(it feels like an elephant is sitting on my chest). Even now I am just sitting on my couch and having some difficulty breathing. It's not impossible for me to breathe, I just slight discomfort and have to work a little harder than a normal person. 

I've always tried working out, push through the shortness of breathe, thinking I'd eventually get used to it, but I've been doing mild workouts (brisk walking, pilates) for 2 years and the shortness of breathe persists. I can't even advance my workouts because I get so out of breathe.

The only history I have is Ulcerative Colitis, I was diagnosed in Jan this year. I take 300mg Lialda every day, no other meds. When I was in the hospital for my UC, I had an anaphylactic reaction to Compazine. My nurse gave me IV benadryl and steroids, and I could instantly breathe *so much easier*. I honestly wouldn't have realized how hard I've been working to breathe if it wasn't for the steroids & benadryl.  

Is this worth bringing up to my doctor? When I was in the hospital, I told my doctors I was short of breathe, but they thought it was from the dehydration and blood loss my UC flare up caused. I tried to explain that I'd had the problem for a while, and was brushed off since I had more acute problems at the time. I felt kind of silly even complaining about it, so I thought I'd ask here and see if it sounds like asthma or some other issue.

title: Safe to Discontinue PPIs with GERD?
selftext:
Age: 28 Sex: Male Height: 6’ 2” Weight: 190

10 Years ago I was diagnosed with GERD via an endoscopy. I learned that my LES does not function at all, and stays consistently wide open. After this procedure I was instructed by the GI Doctor to take PPI’s to heal the damage done by my stomachs acid to my esophagus. It was black and burned pretty badly at that time. I followed up over the next few months/years and was told to just keep on the PPIs and follow a good diet, and eating regiment. 

Recently my GP informed me I should see a GI doctor to make sure everything is okay, basically a checkup to see if any more damage has occurred and to check for any early signs of possible complications.

New GI doctor begins consultation by asking questions and pokes around my stomach for a few minutes, still asking questions. GI Dr says that there’s no need to look inside and that unless I’m having symptoms I should be good to go. He also informs me that I should stop taking the PPIs immediately as the risks outweigh the benefits long term. This is the part that confuses me and I need different opinions and advice on. Original GI doctor and all GP visits I’ve had, they ensured I was still taking PPIs. New GI doctor wants me to stop them completely and just live a health life. 

My question is: Is this a smart move and is it going to be safe long term? They certainly warn you about Barrett’s esophagus and the following cancer to it if you don’t take care of yourself, and now they want me to stop the medication.

title: Help me help my peach of a husband
selftext:
My husband (33M, 135lb, 6ft) wakes up in the middle of the night drenched in sweat that smells exactly like canned peach syrup. As much as I love peaches, this can’t be normal. 

He has episodes of confusion, memory loss, and lethargy. His mood is also affected, he gets extremely negative. Sometimes they escalate into dizzy / blackout spells, which resolve after sitting down and having a snack and water.

No official diagnoses because he really doesn’t like hospitals and medical procedures. Doesn’t drink often, no drugs, not much exercise other than running after a toddler all day.

About 6 years ago he had an infected wound and had to take a heavy dose of antibiotics: that’s when the issues started. He had urinary and gut problems immediately after the antibiotics. A few months later, very suddenly, he started losing consciousness whenever he ate high glycemic index foods. Eventually we managed that with very slow reintroduction to complex carbohydrates and a B complex multivitamin. (Thiamine malabsorption?). The hospital didn’t find anything wrong: he walked out after blood tests and an EKG came back “normal” and he felt “fine”. Family doctors suggested hormonal tests (which we did and came back normal) or something something pancreas. This was all a few years ago so I don’t remember the details: I just know that there was no indication that something was wrong.

He generally feels better when he takes a B complex / multivitamin, but he doesn’t want to take them daily and wants to solve it with more natural solutions like diet or fixing his gut microbiome. Doesn’t want to spend money or time on this, just ignore it, eat an apple a day, and keep going. But I can’t ignore it: the bed stinks of peaches.

After a few months of dry bedsheets, he’s starting to sweat at night and black out in the day again. He’s not taking vitamins but he says “I’m eating lots of meat, I should have enough thiamin.”

I’m worried about his health and want to help him, but I know he has some level of medical trauma that makes him turn into a wall when I mention checking anything. What could it be? Where can I even start? I would really appreciate any advice.

title: Complications after Sebaceous cyst removal
selftext:
24 Male, 83 kg / 183 lbs, 187 cm, surgical removal of sebaceous cyst under scrotum 5 days ago, healthy and fit, clindamycin (antibiotics) and morphine post-surgery - no other meds or conditions

Hello all,

About a year I noticed quite a big cyst-like lump had popped up just under my scrotum (not on it) towards my inner thigh. At the time, I ignored it as I was studying abroad and thought it would disappear. After some weeks, it started swelling heavily and causing great discomfort and pain until I managed to squeeze out a yellowish-smelly substance. This sack would fill up continuously and leak out by itself or when squeezed. Some weeks later, this "hole" would pop up at two other places, so I had three "holes" around that were very close to each other. I noticed my skin trying to pull this up and fold on each other but this yellowish substance would still ooze through. 
Anyway, this process would vary in intensity with a lot of leaking at times and sometimes none for weeks. 

Upon returning back home, this problem seemed to have faded until early Spring when it would start again with the swelling and leaking. One time it got really bad and I went to the emergency as the local health centre was fully booked up. The doctor there said that it was not a testicular cyst or related to the penis and for me to seek expertise via my health centre (that is how it works here). After succeeding in getting a time there, the doctor said this was beyond his capability and that I needed further expert inspection and sent a referral to a renowned skin clinic. 

Meeting the doctor/surgeon there in August, he said that surgical removal of this area and sebaceous gland would be the option to go. Due to a new job and timings, I managed to get a time this Wednesday (5 days ago). The procedure took about 30 mins, he perfomed it alone (?) and he injected local anesthesia removed a thumb-like size of my skin and stitched it back. It was not painful as I got more local anaesthesia upon feeling a sharp pain. There was a lot of blood as he cleaned it up with multiple paper towels and I could see the working table and my seat upon getting up. I was informed that it could of course be sensitive and to take it easy and eat paracetamol upon pain.
Bleeding could also happen but I was supposed to compress it and it would stop.  
I returned to work due to meetings where a slight pain had started but I did not think of it during the meeting. I started to feel wet which went all the way to my knees - this is 2 hours post-surgery. Also, the pain intensifies seriously.  I rushed to the bathroom and noticed lots of blood all over my boxers and pants. 
Notice, I am not afraid at all of blood and gladly watch needles get injected and blood pumped out when I donate blood. I start to clean all the blood but see it is still oozing out at a respectable rate. I compress it for 10 minutes but the bleeding has not stopped. I start feeling super dizzy and get this tinnitus that is out of this world and all lights get blurry, and I lose sense of fingers and toes, I have never passed out in my life but this was going to be it or worse? I managed to pull my pants and get out to throw myself on the sofa in the coffee area where colleagues rushed to my aid. I ask for sugary stuff as they ask what has happened and I try explaining what has happened (I had not told anybody about this as I thought it was a minor thing). They proceeded to call the ambulance while I was still super woozy and "not in this world". Eventually, they manage to take me to a calmer place upon which I have regained a bit of conscience but still struggle to speak and feel. The ambulance comes and takes me to the emergency where my bleeding has stopped and blood work and pressure look good. As I waited for a doctor, I had never in my life felt such pain and discomfort and I must say I am a tough guy, but I was uncontrollably crying out of pain - this is 4 hours post-surgery.

The doctor eventually comes in after 2 hours (the emergency is very slow here...) and says that this is beyond her expertise and she is unsure. For reference, my surgeon is a private clinic that does not share the journal with state-owned hospitals, apparently, and his office was closed at this time of the evening. The doctor proceeded to send me to another emergency in the city. After a chaotic queue and waiting time, the junior doctor was again unsure of what to do as he had noticed a big hard lump had formed around the stitches which was strongly pushing on my left testicle causing pain and making the whole area even more sensitive. A senior doctor examines it too and says that they could open up and empty the lump which is most likely blood that has failed to coagulate. Also, the surgeon seems to have ruptured a blood vessel causing excessive pain and bleeding. As they are not aware of the surgery and do not have access, they tell me to immediately seek my surgeon tomorrow and send me away with painkillers and surgical bandaids. The bleeding is not as intense but comes and goes while the pain is still periodically sharp. I go home at 2 AM-ish and manage to sleep badly for a couple of hours. Upon coming home, I noticed my grey pants' upper part had turned black because of being so drenched in blood even when I had boxers.

In the morning I immediately get in touch with the clinic for which I get a booking in the afternoon at 3 PM. My bleeding has lessened but the pain has not subdued. He also notices the hard lumps and says that the body will take care of these by itself but I say that these are very painful as it pushes on my testicle and makes it feel heavy. He decides to empty these lumps which are three big separate ones now (see pictures). He explains that he will cut open the stitches and empty it and then stitch in a folder like before sewing this again, so like a double loop if that makes sense?
As he injects the anesthesia I scream for every needle, the pain is extreme. Just by pulling or even touching the area, it was super tender. I can see the nurse's worrying looks when I scream and shake. 
They proceed to inject more rounds of anaesthesia but it does not get better and I scream, jump, and shake uncontrollably until more rounds of anaesthesia are injected and the procedure is finally done. 
It took about 45 minutes this time and I could hear the nurse saying "Wow, I can understand it was painful with these forming" referring to the clogged blood. Again, a LOT of blood from what I could see. After the surgery, I felt drained, dead, and completely lifeless. Thinking of it just gives me goosebumps and shivers. I have never felt such pain or reacted so uncontrollably. 

He gave me clindamycin (antibiotics) to use for a week and also morphine for the pain if needed. 
I will have a recheck on Wednesday (a week later) and then get my stitches removed another week later. 

Before the surgery, I was hitting the gym 5-6 days a week and playing basketball 1-2 times a week with quite an active lifestyle. When it comes to eating habits, I am very detail-oriented in nutrition and healthy eating with supplements and other "health habits" and biohacks. I must admit that I do have a form of orthorexia being someone who has lost over 37kgs during my teenage years.

Now to the question and my worries.
Since the procedure, I have felt EXTREMELY drained, tired, and "emotionless"?? I have this extreme hunger even though I barely move or do anything. I cannot concentrate and have difficulties focusing. Is this normal after such a procedure? I eat healthy and balanced but due to cravings and "treatment" I have indulged in more sugary and carbs. I generally consume a good amount of caffeine but now the effect is not nearly as noticeable.

Meeting the doctor/surgeon there in August, he said that surgical removal of this area and sebaceous gland would be the option to go. title: Something's wrong with my eye
selftext:
Age: 27

Sex: Male

Height: 6' 1''

Weight: 330

Race: Native American/Black

Duration: 2 days

Location: Right eye

Medical Conditions: None as far as I know, I was told that I was 'borderline diabetic' a few years ago, but I haven't heard had any symptoms of onset since then. I also wear glasses.

Drugs: No medicine, cigarettes, or alcohol, but I smoked marijuana regularly until May, at which point, I stopped completely.

Photo: [Right Eye](https://imgur.com/a/b3M7QDa) and for comparison [Left Eye](https://imgur.com/a/Yctgt6A)

&#x200B;

Yesterday, I woke up and as I was blinking, I heard a popping sound in my eye, followed by searing pain. I could not open my eye from the pain, and even when it was closed, the pain did not subside. My eye was tearing profusely. It felt like I was being stabbed in my eye, though I could not pinpoint the exact location of the pain in my eye. Eventually the pain subsided and I could open my eye, though it was sore. Later in the day, I heard the popping sound again and the pain was repeated until it stopped. (This process took about an 45 minutes maybe) I thought maybe there was something in my eye, but I checked in a mirror and found nothing. My eye looked normal and was not red at all. I asked my mother about it and she said she thought it was a popped blood vessel, but she wasn't sure. My eye was somewhat sore the rest of the day.

Today I woke up and my eye felt fine, though still somewhat sore. I haven't heard any popping noises, but occasionally, my eye will begin to water and feel pain, coming from the top inner corner. When this happens, my eye instinctively closes and begins tearing. If I lightly hold my eye closed, the pain will be lessened. My eyeball and eyelid both feel sore. 

Note: I do spend a fair amount of time on my computer. I am taking three online courses this summer, as well as working on a novel. I'm not sure if my staring at a screen is the issue, though I doubt it as my computer usage habits have not increased dramatically, in fact, they may have decreased slightly. 

Do you have any idea what is going on, or how I can fix it?

title: Please Help, Small Beads Coming out of Vulva
selftext:
This is super embarrassing but I have no idea what it could be and I am very worried!
I’m female, 21, about 115 lbs and 5ft 5inches. No history of smoking or any medical conditions. I am not on any medication.
I’ve had what I thought was an ingrown hair next to my vaginal opening for some time now. I tried to remove it previously but it was stubborn and I would need to break skin to get to it. title: Excessive thirst at night (not diabetes)
selftext:
30M, 6' 80kg, south Indian. I've had this condition for the past 7-8 months or so. I'd go to sleep between 12 and 1 AM as normal. Starting around 3-4, I'd wake up maybe once every half an hour to an hour with my throat parched and my mouth dry, and I'd have to take a sip of water. Altogether I'd wake up 6-7 times though I have no trouble falling asleep immediately. I've gone through an entire 1L bottle of water in a night without having to pee in between. This has also worsened over time - earlier I'd have to drink less water and I'd also wake up to pee because I was drinking so much. Nowadays i can hold the pee and when I go in the morning it's still a little yellow. This is far far worse when I've had some alcohol the night before (maybe 2-3 beers, that's it, and maybe once every couple of weeks) - I'd wake up as much as 10-15 times. 

Diabetes is the first thing which comes up when I Google this and that's what my doc thought too..she recommended a blood sugar test which ruled it out. For reference: 

80 mg/dL fasting 
74 mg/dL post prandial
5.2% HBA1C
102.5 mg/dL estimated average glucose 

She's out of ideas other than telling me to hydrate myself through the day and eat healthy. And she kinda ruled out sleep apnea too saying it's unlikely since I'm not overweight. To be fair it's the free clinic on my campus. 

What could it be? I've noticed i drool a lot during sleep - could that be it? But why specifically should the thirst begin a little later into my sleep and not from the start? And what reasons could there be for sleeping with my mouth open? I've been told I breathe loud, and that I snore sometimes. Still doesn't explain why it started now. 

I'm out of ideas other than going for a (possibly expensive) sleep apnea test. Any contraptions to keep the mouth closed during the night? Fortunately this doesn't cause me to be excessively sleepy during daytime, any more than I've been in the past. 

Any ideas? Thanks!
